terms.definition: A tiny living organism made of a single cell, with no nucleus.
terms.function: A single living thing that can grow, feed, and reproduce.
terms.whereItIs: Almost everywhere - soil, water, air, and our bodies.
terms.whyItMatters: They are the most common life form and shape our health and the planet.

terms.definition: The way a bacterium reproduces by copying its DNA and splitting in two.
terms.function: Turns one cell into two identical cells.
terms.whereItIs: Inside each bacterium as it divides.
terms.whyItMatters: It is how bacteria multiply quickly.

terms.definition: The firm outer layer of a bacterium that protects and shapes it.
terms.whereItIs: At the outer surface of the bacterium.
terms.whyItMatters: It is one reason bacteria are tough.

terms.definition: Bacteria that are helpful, such as those that help digest food or make yogurt.
terms.function: Help our bodies and make useful food products.
terms.whereItIs: In our gut, the soil, and foods like yogurt.
terms.whyItMatters: Most bacteria are harmless or beneficial, not disease-causing.
